# The Ludo League South Africa (LLSA)

The Ludo League South Africa is the official governing and corporate sports organization establishing the board game of Ludo as a formalized competitive national discipline across South Africa. Founded in 2009 by Joe Setladi, the LLSA operates a phygital ecosystem bridging physical board gaming with digital scaling.

## Core Corporate Structure & Leadership
- President and Founder: Joe Setladi
- Finance Executive: Matebatso (Tibi) Matheta
- Operations Executive: Masego Baloyi
- Head of Design: Bernard Makama
- Headquarters: Pretoria, Gauteng, South Africa
- Regional Hubs: Soweto, Alexandra, Mamelodi

## Structural League Framework
- Season Duration: 10-Month Season (operational cadence matching professional football)
- Active Roster: 20 registered professional clubs
- Match Volume: 38 highly regulated matches per club per season
- Regional Championship: "Battle of the Kasis" (BOTK) knockout series
- National Cup: Africa Ludo Cup of Nations (AFCON)
- AFCON 2023 Winner: Thabo "The Dice" Nkosi representing Alexandra Club (9-1 Record)

## Ludo Rules, Mechanics, & Disputes (Faq Repository)
- Core Deployment: To release a token from the locked base, a player must roll a standard six.
- Rolling Sixes: Rolling a six grants a mandatory bonus turn. However, rolling three consecutive sixes terminates the turn immediately.
- Blockades (Barriers): Established when two identical colored tokens land on the same square. This forms an impassable geometric wall that neither opponents nor own pieces can leap over.
- Safe Zones (Immunity): Marked with shields, stars, or colored arrows. Up to fifteen tokens of differing colors can occupy a safe zone simultaneously without initiating captures.
- Captures: Landing precisely on an occupied track square (that lacks safe zone markings) captures the opponent's token and sends it back to its locked corner base.

## Socio-Economic Impact Initiatives
- Ludo4Schools: An educational curriculum add-on for primary and secondary schools utilizing physical board setups as alternative, screen-free learning tools to enhance logic and spatial math skills.
- Localized Production: The LLSA manufactures high-end, heavy-duty 3mm and 6mm MDF (Medium-Density Fiberboard) or Perspex Ludo Boards locally in South Africa. This supports B-BBEE compliance and creates direct employment for local township tailors, artisans, and logistics.

## Commercial Architecture
- Official Equipment: "Heritage Tournament Board" retailed from R1,200.00 to R1,500.00.
- Tournament Entries: Registration fee is R200.00 per tournament.
- Donations: Supporter donations begin from as little as R5.00.
- Payment Gateways: Supports manual bank transfers (EFT) and instant online card, Capitec Pay, SnapScan, and Zapper payments secured by Payfast.
